Docs: [AWS provider authentication](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/aws/latest/docs#authentication-and-configuration), [AWS default_tags](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/aws/latest/docs#default_tags-configuration-block), [Debugging](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/internals/debugging), [Environment variables](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/v1.6.x/config/environment-variables), [Dependency lock file](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/v1.6.x/files/dependency-lock), [Providers within modules](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/v1.6.x/modules/develop/providers)

lessons.title: 6a. HCP Terraform runs
lessons.markdown:
## 1. Three run workflows

| Workflow | Config comes from | Runs start when | Typical use |
|---|---|---|---|
| VCS-driven (UI/VCS) | Linked repo branch, via webhook | Commit/merge to the linked branch; PR opens a speculative plan; manual **+ New run** | Default, review in PRs |
| CLI-driven | Local directory, uploaded by `terraform plan`/`apply` | You run the CLI with a `cloud` block | Developers, existing CI |
| API-driven | Your tool uploads a `.tar.gz` configuration version | Upload finishes (run is created automatically) | Custom pipelines, unsupported VCS |

```hcl
terraform {
  cloud {
    organization = "my-org"
    workspaces {
      project = "networking"
      name    = "net-prod"   # or tags = { layer = "networking" }, not both
    }
  }
}
```

- Run `terraform login`, then `terraform init`. A missing workspace (or project) is created on `init`.
- CLI `terraform plan` = remote **speculative** plan. It uses local code but the workspace's variables.
- CLI `terraform apply` is **not allowed** on VCS-linked workspaces. The repo is the source of truth: merge to the branch instead.
- The `cloud` block needs Terraform 1.1+. Older versions use `backend "remote"`.
- Use `.terraformignore` to exclude files from the CLI upload.
- A manual UI run uses the current configuration version. It does not fetch the latest commit.
- A new VCS workspace needs one manual run before webhooks start runs.

## 2. Run stages

Order of a run (stages only run if configured):

| # | Stage | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Pending | Waits in the workspace queue until earlier runs finish |
| 2 | Pre-plan run tasks | External check on the configuration |
| 3 | Plan | `terraform plan`. Fails → **Plan Errored** |
| 4 | Post-plan run tasks | External check, gets the plan JSON |
| 5 | OPA policy evaluation | Before cost estimation |
| 6 | Cost estimation | Estimates resource costs |
| 7 | Sentinel policy check | After cost estimation |
| 8 | Pre-apply run tasks | Only for confirmed runs |
| 9 | Apply | `terraform apply` → **Applied** or **Apply Errored** |
| 10 | Post-apply run tasks | Advisory only, can't stop anything |

- Plan with no changes → **Planned and Finished**. Nothing is applied.
- Waiting for approval → **Needs Confirmation** (or **Policy Checked**). Someone with **Apply runs** confirms or discards.
- While a plan waits for confirmation, no other run can start in that workspace.
- A run is locked to its configuration version and variable values. Later changes only affect future runs.

## 3. Speculative plans, auto-apply, run triggers

**Speculative (plan-only) plans**
- Can never be applied. Still run policy checks and run tasks.
- Skip the run queue and ignore workspace locks.
- Started by: opening/updating a PR against the linked branch, `terraform plan` from the CLI, **Plan only** in the UI, or the API.
- PRs from **forks** don't trigger speculative plans (on HCP Terraform).
- Can use a different Terraform version than the workspace, to test an upgrade.

**Auto-apply**

| Run source | Auto-applies? |
|---|---|
| VCS commit, UI, API | Yes, if workspace **Auto-apply** is on |
| CLI `terraform apply` | Only with `-auto-approve` |
| Run trigger | Only if **Auto-apply run triggers** is on (separate setting) |
| Queued by a user without Apply permission | No, someone with Apply must confirm |
| Saved plan (`plan -out`) | Never |

**Run triggers**
- Queue a run in this workspace after a **successful apply** in a source workspace.
- Up to 20 source workspaces. Configuring needs admin on the target workspace plus read runs on the source.
- Use them when this workspace reads another workspace's outputs (e.g. app reads VPC IDs from network).

## 4. Run modes

| Mode | CLI | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Plan and apply (standard) | `terraform apply` | Plan, then apply after confirmation |
| Plan only | `terraform plan` | Speculative, never applied |
| Refresh-only | `plan/apply -refresh-only` | Updates state to match real objects. Changes no infrastructure |
| Destroy | `terraform destroy` | Plans to destroy everything |
| Replace | `-replace=ADDR` | Forces replacement of one resource |
| Target | `-target=ADDR` | Exceptional use. Disables cost estimation |
| Saved plan | `plan -out` + `apply FILE` | CLI 1.6+. Never auto-applied. Discarded if state changes first |
| Allow empty apply | UI/API | Apply with no changes, e.g. to upgrade state format |

`terraform import` (the command) never runs remotely. It runs locally against the workspace state, so workspace environment variables aren't available. Prefer `import` blocks.

## 5. Locking

| Fact | Detail |
|---|---|
| Effect | New runs can be queued but don't start until unlock |
| Ignored by | Plan-only runs and the plan stage of saved plans |
| Who can lock | **Lock/unlock workspace** permission (Write and Admin roles) |
| Unlock someone else's lock | Only a workspace **admin** (force unlock) |
| State upload | Workspace must be locked by the uploading user |
| Automatic lock | A running run locks the workspace |

## 6. Execution modes

| Mode | Where Terraform runs | Workspace variables used? | HCP features |
|---|---|---|---|
| Remote (default) | HCP Terraform's disposable VMs | Yes | Policies, cost estimation, run tasks, notifications, VCS |
| Local | Your machine or CI | **No**, workspace only stores state | Remote-run features off |
| Agent | Your self-hosted agent (outbound-only connection) | Yes | Like Remote, but reaches private networks |

- Default is **Project Default** (project inherits the organization default).
- Local mode needs a token with **Read and write state** and **Lock/unlock**.
- Agents are a paid feature. Pick them for private/on-prem targets without opening inbound access.

Docs: [Remote operations](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cloud-docs/run/remote-operations), [Run states and stages](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cloud-docs/run/states), [Run modes and options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cloud-docs/run/modes-and-options), [CLI-driven runs](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cloud-docs/run/cli), [UI/VCS-driven runs](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cloud-docs/run/ui), [API-driven runs](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cloud-docs/run/api), [Run triggers](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cloud-docs/workspaces/settings/run-triggers), [Workspace settings](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cloud-docs/workspaces/settings)

lessons.title: 6b. Workspaces, variables and access
lessons.markdown:
## 1. Organizations, projects, workspaces

| Level | Holds | Key facts |
|---|---|---|
| Organization | Projects, teams, policy sets, run tasks, private registry, VCS connections | **Owners** team has all permissions |
| Project | Workspaces | Every workspace is in exactly **one** project. **Default Project** can't be deleted |
| Workspace | Config, state, variables, run history | Acts like a separate working directory |

**HCP Terraform workspace vs CLI workspace**

| | HCP Terraform workspace | CLI workspace (`terraform workspace`) |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose | Separate config, state, variables, permissions | Several states for **one** config in one directory |
| Required | Yes | No |
| Access control | Yes, per team | No |

## 2. Workspace settings

| Setting | What to know |
|---|---|
| Terraform version | Exact version or constraint. Default: latest release when the workspace was created |
| Working directory | Relative path in the repo where Terraform runs. In VCS workspaces, only changes there trigger runs by default |
| Execution mode | Project Default, Remote, Local, Agent |
| Auto-apply | Off by default. Separate toggle for run-trigger runs |
| VCS trigger | Branch, path filters, or Git tags |
| Health | Drift detection and continuous validation |
| Remote state sharing | Who may read this workspace's state |

Changing settings needs workspace **admin**.

## 3. Variables

| Category | Use for | HCL option | How Terraform gets it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Terraform variable | Values for `variable` blocks | Yes, for lists/maps | Input variable |
| Environment variable | Provider credentials, `TF_LOG`, `TF_CLI_ARGS_*` | No | `export` in the run shell |

- **Sensitive** = write-only. Nobody can read it in the UI or API, including admins. You can only set a new value.
- Sensitive Terraform variables can still end up in state or logs if the config outputs them. Prefer environment variables for credentials.
- Descriptions are not encrypted.
- `*.auto.tfvars` and `terraform.tfvars` in the config are used but not shown in the UI.
- Local `AWS_*` environment variables are **not** sent to a remote run. Set credentials in the workspace.
- Local execution mode ignores workspace variables and variable sets.

## 4. Variable sets and precedence

A variable set is a reusable group of variables.

| Scope | Applies to |
|---|---|
| Global | All current and future workspaces in the organization |
| Project | All current and future workspaces in chosen projects |
| Workspace | Chosen workspaces |

- Owned by the organization (needs owners, **Manage all projects** or **Manage all workspaces**) or by a project (needs project-level **Manage variable sets**, or Write/Maintain/Admin on the project).
- **Priority** variable set: beats every more specific value, including `-var`.

Precedence, highest first:

| # | Source |
|---|---|
| 1 | Priority variable sets (global > project > workspace scope) |
| 2 | CLI `-var` / `-var-file` |
| 3 | Local `TF_VAR_*` (CLI workflow) |
| 4 | **Workspace-specific variables** |
| 5 | Normal variable sets: project-owned before org-owned, workspace-scoped before project-scoped |
| 6 | Global variable sets |
| 7 | `*.auto.tfvars` |
| 8 | `terraform.tfvars` |

- Same key in two sets of the same scope → the **lexically first name wins** (`A_set` beats `B_set`), not the newest edit.
- To override a set's value for one workspace, create a workspace variable with the same key and category. The UI marks the set's value **OVERWRITTEN**.
- Global sets can't share a key with another global set.

## 5. Teams and permissions

Permissions go to **teams**, never to single users. They are **additive**: the highest grant from any level wins.

**Workspace roles**

| Permission | Read | Plan | Write | Admin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Read runs, variables, state | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Queue plans | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Apply runs | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Write variables, write state | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Lock/unlock, download Sentinel mocks | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Manage workspace run tasks | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Settings, team access, delete workspace | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |

- **Custom** workspace role: pick any non-admin permission. Example: apply runs but no state read, or **Read outputs only** state access.
- **Project roles**: Read, Write, Maintain (+ create/delete workspaces), Admin (+ project settings, team access, move workspaces), or Custom. They apply to all workspaces in the project.
- **Organization permissions**: e.g. View/Manage all projects, View/Manage all workspaces, Manage policies, Manage policy overrides, Manage run tasks, Manage VCS settings, Manage modules/providers.
- **Owners** team: every permission. Some actions are owner-only, e.g. organization health settings.
- Anyone who can merge to a VCS-linked branch can indirectly queue runs.

## 6. Remote state sharing

| Option | Who can read the state |
|---|---|
| Share with specific workspaces (**default**, list empty) | Only listed workspaces |
| Share with all workspaces in this project | Same project |
| Share with all workspaces in this organization | Everyone in the org |

- Needed for the `terraform_remote_state` data source against this workspace.
- Prefer the `tfe_outputs` data source (tfe provider). It reads outputs only, not the full state.
- For users, **Read outputs only** state permission is enough for `terraform output` and `terraform_remote_state`.

## 7. Health assessments

| Check | Finds |
|---|---|
| Drift detection | Real infrastructure no longer matches the configuration |
| Continuous validation | `check` blocks, preconditions, postconditions that now fail (needs TF 1.3+) |

- Paid tier (Standard/Premium).
- Runs periodically (e.g. every 24 hours) in Remote or Agent mode only. Needs a successful apply first. Paused after an errored run.
- Never changes infrastructure or state, never blocks runs.
- Workspace admin enables it or starts an on-demand check. Organization owners can enforce it org-wide.
- Fix drift: apply a normal run to revert, or update the config to accept the change.

Docs: [Workspaces](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cloud-docs/workspaces), [Projects](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cloud-docs/projects), [Workspace settings](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cloud-docs/workspaces/settings), [Variables](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cloud-docs/variables), [Manage variables](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cloud-docs/variables/managing-variables), [Permissions](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cloud-docs/users-teams-organizations/permissions), [Workspace permissions](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cloud-docs/users-teams-organizations/permissions/workspace), [Project permissions](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cloud-docs/users-teams-organizations/permissions/project), [Health](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cloud-docs/workspaces/health)

lessons.title: 6c–6d. Credentials and governance
lessons.markdown:
## 1. Static credentials

| Approach | How | Downside |
|---|---|---|
| Workspace env variables | `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` as **sensitive environment** variables | Long-lived keys, rotate by hand per workspace |
| Variable set | Same variables in one set, scoped to a project or many workspaces | One place to rotate, still long-lived |
| Terraform variables | `variable "secret_key"` | Avoid. Values can leak into state, logs and Sentinel mocks |

- Use **environment** category, not Terraform category, for credentials.
- Mark them **sensitive** (write-only).
- Never hardcode keys in the provider block.
- A workspace-specific variable with the same key overrides the set, e.g. a different account for one workspace.

## 2. Dynamic provider credentials (AWS OIDC)

Per run, HCP Terraform creates a signed OIDC **workload identity token**. AWS verifies it and returns **temporary** credentials. They are discarded when the plan/apply ends.

**AWS side**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| IAM OIDC identity provider | URL `https://app.terraform.io`, audience `aws.workload.identity` |
| IAM role trust policy | `Action: sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`, `Principal.Federated` = OIDC provider ARN |
| Condition `app.terraform.io:aud` | `aws.workload.identity` |
| Condition `app.terraform.io:sub` | `organization:ORG:project:PROJECT:workspace:WS:run_phase:plan` or `apply` (`StringLike` with `*` for wildcards) |
| Permissions policy | What the role may do in AWS |

Always check at least `aud` and the organization name in `sub`. Otherwise other organizations could assume the role.

**HCP Terraform side** (environment variables, on the workspace or in a variable set):

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `TFC_AWS_PROVIDER_AUTH` | `true` (required, otherwise no OIDC auth) |
| `TFC_AWS_RUN_ROLE_ARN` | Role ARN to assume (required unless both plan/apply roles are set) |
| `TFC_AWS_PLAN_ROLE_ARN` / `TFC_AWS_APPLY_ROLE_ARN` | Optional: read-only role for plan, write role for apply |
| `TFC_AWS_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_AUDIENCE` | Optional, custom `aud` |

- The provider block sets only `region` (or `AWS_REGION`). Remove other auth arguments, they interfere.
- Agents need v1.7.0+.

**Why it beats static keys**

| Static keys | Dynamic credentials |
|---|---|
| Long-lived, leakable | Valid only for one plan/apply |
| Manual rotation | Nothing to rotate |
| Same rights for plan and apply | Separate roles per run phase |
| Any holder can use them | Trust policy limits to org/project/workspace |

## 3. Policy sets

Policies check the **plan** before apply. A **policy set** groups policies of one framework.

| Scope of a policy set | Effect |
|---|---|
| Global | All workspaces in the organization |
| Projects | All workspaces in selected projects |
| Workspaces | Selected workspaces |
| Tags | Workspaces with matching tags |
| Exclusions | Skip specific workspaces/projects |

- One framework per set (Sentinel **or** OPA). A workspace can have sets of both.
- Sources: VCS repo (recommended, policy as code), API/`tfe_policy_set`, UI, pre-written library.
- Free tier: one policy set with up to five policies. VCS-connected sets need a paid tier.
- Creating policies needs the org **Manage policies** permission.
- Runs order: **OPA** before cost estimation. **Sentinel** policy checks after cost estimation, so they can use cost data.
- Speculative plans run policies too, so PR authors see failures before merging.
- Policies need remote or agent execution. Local mode skips them.

## 4. Enforcement levels and overrides

| Framework | Level | Failed policy |
|---|---|---|
| Sentinel | `advisory` | Warning, run continues |
| Sentinel | `soft-mandatory` | Run stops in **Policy Override**. Authorized user can override |
| Sentinel | `hard-mandatory` | Run stops (**Plan Errored**). Fix the code or the policy |
| OPA | `advisory` | Warning, run continues |
| OPA | `mandatory` | Run stops. User with **Manage policy overrides** can override |

**Who can override**

| Permission | Effect |
|---|---|
| Organization owners | Always |
| Team with **Manage policy overrides** | Override in all workspaces (also gets read on all workspaces) |
| Team with **Delegate policy overrides** | Override only where a project/workspace admin enabled **Allow policy overrides** |

- Discarding a run needs **Apply runs**. Overriding needs override permission.
- Exception: a Sentinel set using **policy evaluations** with "can be overridden" enabled also allows overriding hard-mandatory failures.
- Need a rule nobody can bypass? Sentinel `hard-mandatory`.

## 5. Run tasks

Run tasks send run data to an external service (security scan, cost tool, HCP Packer check). The service replies passed/failed.

| Stage | Gets | Can block? |
|---|---|---|
| Pre-plan | Configuration version | Yes |
| Post-plan | Plan JSON | Yes |
| Pre-apply | Configuration version (confirmed runs only) | Yes |
| Post-apply | Run data | No, advisory only |

| Enforcement | Failure (incl. 10-minute timeout) |
|---|---|
| Advisory | Run continues with a warning |
| Mandatory | Run errors |

- Created at org level (**Manage run tasks**). Attached per workspace (**Manage workspace run tasks**, workspace admin) or scoped to org/projects.
- Optional **HMAC key** lets the service verify requests.
- Policy vs run task: policy = rules on the plan inside HCP Terraform. Run task = third-party tool via webhook.

## 6. Private registry

- Share modules and providers only inside the organization. Versioned, with docs.
- Source format: `app.terraform.io/<ORG>/<NAME>/<PROVIDER>`, e.g. `app.terraform.io/example_corp/vpc/aws`.
- `localterraform.com` is a generic hostname that resolves to the current instance.
- Public modules/providers can be added to the private registry to mark them as approved.
- Publishing needs **Manage modules** / **Manage providers**.
- Enforce usage with a Sentinel policy (e.g. only modules from the private registry).

`profile = "111122223333"`, with no shared config file on the CI runner

questions.explanation: `assume_role` uses the credentials from the chain (here env vars) to get credentials for the target account. Default values in code are hardcoded secrets. A profile needs a shared config file, and `default_tags` doesn't change identity.

questions.situation: Both `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`/`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` and a `[default]` profile in `~/.aws/credentials` are present. The provider block sets only `region`.
questions.question: Which credentials does the AWS provider use?

options.text: The EC2 instance profile, because it is checked first
None; Terraform fails because the sources are ambiguous

questions.explanation: Environment variables come before the shared credentials file in the AWS provider's lookup order. The instance profile is checked last. Multiple sources aren't an error; the first match wins.

questions.situation: `terraform apply` fails while creating an AWS resource. You want only the AWS provider's API calls in a file, at debug level.
questions.question: Which environment variables do you set?
questions.explanation: `TF_LOG_PROVIDER` limits logging to provider plugins, and `TF_LOG_PATH` writes to a file. `TF_LOG_CORE` logs only Core. `TF_LOG_PATH` alone enables nothing, and `PROVIDER` isn't a log level.

questions.situation: You deleted the `provider "aws" { alias = "west" … }` block, together with the resource blocks that used it. You haven't applied yet. `terraform plan` now fails with `Provider configuration not present`.
questions.question: What do you do?

options.text: Re-add the `aws.west` provider block, apply so the resources are destroyed, then remove the provider block
Run `terraform init -upgrade` to reinstall the provider
Add `aws.west` to `configuration_aliases` in the root module

questions.explanation: Terraform needs the original provider configuration to destroy objects still in state. Re-add the block, destroy the objects, then remove the block. The problem isn't the installed plugin or the lock file, and `configuration_aliases` is for child modules.

questions.situation: A workspace is linked to the `main` branch of a GitHub repo. A developer runs `terraform apply` locally with a matching `cloud` block.
questions.question: What happens?

options.text: HCP Terraform rejects the apply; changes must be merged to `main`
The apply runs remotely using the local configuration
The apply runs locally and uploads the new state
A speculative plan runs and waits for confirmation

questions.explanation: Remote CLI applies are not allowed in VCS-linked workspaces because the repo is the source of truth. `terraform plan` would work (speculative), but `apply` is refused rather than run remotely or locally.

questions.situation: A workspace has cost estimation, a Sentinel policy set and an OPA policy set enabled.
questions.question: In which order do these stages run after the plan?

options.text: OPA policy evaluation, cost estimation, Sentinel policy check
Cost estimation, OPA policy evaluation, Sentinel policy check
Sentinel policy check, OPA policy evaluation, cost estimation
Sentinel and OPA run together before the plan, then cost estimation

questions.explanation: OPA runs before cost estimation and Sentinel policy checks run after it, so Sentinel can use cost data. Policies always evaluate a finished plan, never before it.

questions.situation: Workspace `app` has Auto-apply enabled and a run trigger on workspace `network`. After `network` applies, a run is queued in `app` but waits for confirmation.
questions.question: Why?

options.text: Run-trigger runs only auto-apply if **Auto-apply run triggers** is also enabled
Run-trigger runs are always speculative plans
The `network` workspace must share its state with `app` first
Auto-apply only works for runs started from the CLI

questions.explanation: Run-triggered runs have their own auto-apply setting, separate from the main one. They are real runs, not speculative, and state sharing affects reading outputs, not auto-apply.

questions.situation: An engineer locked a production workspace for maintenance. A teammate opens a pull request against the linked branch.
questions.question: What happens to the PR's speculative plan?

options.text: It runs normally, because plan-only runs ignore workspace locks
It waits in Pending until the workspace is unlocked
It fails immediately with a lock error
It runs, then waits for the lock owner to confirm it

questions.explanation: Plan-only runs can't change state or infrastructure, so they skip the queue and ignore locks. Normal runs would be queued and wait for the unlock.

questions.situation: Your AWS resources sit in a private VPC with no inbound internet access. You want remote runs with policy checks and workspace variables.
questions.question: Which execution mode do you choose?

options.text: Agent, with HCP Terraform agents in the private network
Local, running Terraform from a CI runner in the VPC
Remote, after allowing HCP Terraform's IPs inbound
Remote with a VPN workspace variable

questions.explanation: Agents connect outbound only and still give remote-run features like policies and workspace variables. Local mode would drop workspace variables and policy checks, and Remote needs inbound access you don't want.

questions.situation: A project-scoped variable set sets `instance_type = "t3.small"`. A workspace in that project has a workspace-specific Terraform variable `instance_type = "t3.large"`. No set is priority.
questions.question: Which value does a VCS-triggered run use?

options.text: `t3.large`, because workspace-specific variables beat non-priority variable sets
`t3.small`, because variable sets are applied last
The run fails because of a duplicate key
Whichever value was edited most recently

questions.explanation: Workspace-specific variables override normal variable sets, and the UI marks the set's value as OVERWRITTEN. Only a priority variable set would beat the workspace value; duplicates don't fail and edit time doesn't matter.

questions.situation: Junior engineers should queue plans in a workspace, but every apply must be approved by the platform team.
questions.question: Which workspace role do you give the junior team?
questions.explanation: Plan lets them queue plans but not apply runs. Read can't queue plans, and Write or Admin would let them apply.

questions.situation: Workspace `app` uses `terraform_remote_state` to read VPC outputs from a new workspace `network` in another project. The run fails with an access error.
questions.question: What do you change?

options.text: In `network`, add `app` to **Share with specific workspaces**
Move both workspaces into the same organization

questions.explanation: New workspaces share state with no one by default; `network` must allow `app`. A run trigger only queues runs, and they're already in the same organization.

questions.situation: You set up the IAM OIDC provider and role for HCP Terraform. Runs still fail with "no valid credential sources".
questions.question: Which workspace configuration is missing?

options.text: `assume_role_with_web_identity` with a static token in the provider block

questions.explanation: HCP Terraform only requests OIDC credentials when `TFC_AWS_PROVIDER_AUTH` is `true` and a role ARN is set, as environment variables. Static keys would bypass OIDC, and extra auth arguments in the provider block interfere with it.

questions.situation: Security wants plans to use a read-only role and applies to use a write role, without static keys.
questions.question: What do you configure?

options.text: Two IAM roles with trust policies matching `run_phase:plan` and `run_phase:apply`, set via `TFC_AWS_PLAN_ROLE_ARN` and `TFC_AWS_APPLY_ROLE_ARN`
One role with `run_phase:*` and two Terraform variables for the policies
Two variable sets with different `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` values
A Sentinel policy that blocks writes during the plan phase

questions.explanation: The `sub` claim includes the run phase, so separate roles per phase need separate trust policies and the plan/apply role variables. A `run_phase:*` wildcard gives both phases the same role, and static keys are what you want to avoid.

questions.situation: A Sentinel policy must block untagged resources. Team leads should be able to let an urgent run through after review.
questions.question: Which setup fits?

options.text: `soft-mandatory`, and give the leads' team **Manage policy overrides**
`hard-mandatory`, and give the leads' team workspace Admin
`advisory`, and give the leads' team Apply runs
`soft-mandatory`, and give the leads' team workspace Write

questions.explanation: Soft-mandatory failures can be overridden by users with override permission. Hard-mandatory blocks the run for everyone, advisory never blocks, and workspace roles like Write or Admin don't include overriding policies.

questions.situation: You want a third-party security scanner to review the plan JSON and stop the run if it finds critical issues.
questions.question: What do you configure?

options.text: A post-plan run task with enforcement level Mandatory
A post-apply run task with enforcement level Mandatory
A pre-plan run task with enforcement level Advisory
An OPA policy set with enforcement level advisory

questions.explanation: Post-plan tasks receive the plan JSON, and Mandatory failures stop the run. Post-apply tasks can't block anything, pre-plan tasks only see the configuration, and advisory levels never block.

questions.situation: In the exam lab (Terraform 1.6.6) you must stop managing `aws_s3_bucket.logs` with Terraform without deleting the bucket.
questions.question: What works?

options.text: `terraform state rm aws_s3_bucket.logs`, then remove the resource block
Remove the resource block and run `terraform apply`

questions.explanation: `removed` blocks arrive in Terraform 1.7, so in 1.6 you use `terraform state rm`. C and D both destroy the bucket.

questions.situation: In Terraform 1.6 you want to import three existing subnets with `import` blocks.
questions.question: How do you write them?

options.text: One `import` block with `for_each` over the subnet IDs

questions.explanation: `for_each` on `import` blocks needs Terraform 1.7. `terraform import` has no `-all` (C), and `-refresh-only` (D) only updates state for resources already managed.

questions.situation: The exam tests Terraform 1.6.
questions.question: Which feature can you use there?
questions.explanation: `import` blocks and config generation exist since 1.5. Provider-defined functions (1.8), ephemeral resources (1.10) and `removed` blocks (1.7) don't exist in 1.6.
